title: 8-year backtested crypto trend system: what improved it, what didn't, looking for criticism
author: lks777
selftext:
I've been building a trend-following system for crypto and I'd like honest criticism before moving it to real money. It's currently running on a demo account.

The core idea

Signal: go long when the daily DMI (DI+ / DI−) crosses up. It's checked at every 8H close, with no lookahead.

Exit: when the daily DI flips back. At +1R the stop moves to break-even and the whole position runs.

Complementary strategies: an 8H Supertrend (longs and shorts, half risk) and a short-only support-breakdown strategy.

Market: 7 major cryptos, with fees and funding included in every test.

How I test ideas

Two groups of coins: an idea is only accepted if it improves results on the 7 system coins and on 15 coins never used for design.

Random control: any idea that changes position size is compared against the same sizing shuffled at random.

Inflated costs: stress tests with fees and slippage far above normal.

What improved it (image 2)

Removing "rebound" entries, which lost money on their own.

Placing the stop at the low of the whole previous bearish DI phase instead of the previous candle's low. Fewer noise stop-outs and a smaller max drawdown.

Adding the Supertrend as a second strategy. Its shorts make money exactly in the longs' bad months.

What I tested that did NOT work (70+ tests):

Lower or higher timeframes: none beat the daily signal read on 8H.

Entry confirmations (breakout of the signal high, pullbacks, structure, split entries): all worse. The best trades take off immediately.

ICT (ORB + FVG, liquidity sweeps, CRT) and moving-average crosses: negative after costs.

Time stops, volatility-based sizing, regime filters (BTC vs its 200-day average): all made it worse.

What worries me (image 3)

Concentrated profits: the best 10 months make up 69% of the total, and some years are almost flat.

Weaker on unseen coins: on the unseen coins the system is still profitable, but clearly weaker than on the system coins.

Still unconfirmed: I have a signal "quality" score (distance to moving averages, compression, volume) that looks helpful. I'm logging it on demo before using it.

Questions:

What validation would you add before going live?

Is it reasonable for a trend system to depend this much on a few months?

How do you handle flat years without abandoning the system?

comments.author: PalatableDewey_0
comments.body: The random sizing controls and testing on 15 additional coins are probably the strongest parts of this approach. I also like that you included funding and higher execution costs instead of assuming perfect fills. The market wagers I explore on Moon are much more discretionary but I'd apply the same skepticism to any promising results. The demo period should help reveal whether those improvements hold outside the original test.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good that you use unseen coins and a random control, and that you share what failed. Profits coming from a few months is normal for trend following, so the real question is whether you can hold through the flat stretches, and that depends on sizing the system so a long flat period doesn't force you out. One caution is that you tried over 70 ideas and each improvement was picked using the same history, so the true test is the demo and fresh data that arrives after today. I'd decide in writing now how long a flat stretch or how deep a drawdown makes you stop. Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance, if you want one more place to compare.

replies.author: lks777
replies.body: Thanks — fully agree. I've written down stop rules today: review at a 20R drawdown, halve risk at 25R, stop and re-evaluate at 35R or if live behavior diverges from the backtest (stop-out rate, slippage). I won't stop for flat periods: the backtest already had ~2-year flat stretches. And yes, the demo plus data from today on is the real out-of-sample test.
